+  [verify: none — <reason>].
+- After `flow freeze` this file is checksum-protected: any edit outside

[verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/references-config.test.ts`]
+- AC2: Without a references file every resolve result, validator verdict and TUI line is byte-identical to flow 461 behaviour. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/context-resolver.test.ts src/gdskills/resolved-context-check.test.ts`]
+- AC3: `resolve-context` accepts the task text (CLI `--task-text`, and the same field in the MCP and flow-orchestrator call) and records it, truncated to a stated limit, in the last-resolve record. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/context-resolver.test.ts -t "task text"`]
+- AC4: A declared reference whose glob matches any task file is resolved as `must_read`, with `reason` naming the glob, plus `anchor`, `description`, `section_bytes` and the sha256 of the whole file. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/context-resolver.test.ts -t "glob promotes"`]
+- AC5: A declared reference whose keyword occurs in the task text, case-insensitively and on a word boundary, is `must_read` with `reason` naming the keyword; a task matching neither stays `on_demand` and keeps its description, anchor and condition in the entry. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/context-resolver.test.ts -t "keyword promotes"`]
+- AC6: With an anchor the obligation and the budget are the section from the heading to the next heading of equal or higher level; a missing anchor makes the entry an error in `check` and falls back to the whole file with a warning at resolve time, never to silence. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/references-section.test.ts`]
+- AC7: A promoted reference is never dropped by the byte cap; when the cap is exceeded the resolver warns with the sizes and keeps the obligation. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/context-resolver.test.ts -t "cap keeps promoted"`]
+- AC8: Documents cited by a rule but not declared keep the flow 461 `on_demand` behaviour and are listed as undeclared in the resolve record. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/context-resolver.test.ts -t "undeclared"`]
+- AC9: The `project_context_applied` item schemas of task-implementer and tests-creator (and their synced copies) accept optional `anchor` and `summary` strings, keep the `how` enum unchanged, and still reject unknown properties; every result valid under flow 461 stays valid. [verify: exec `bun test src/gdskills/output-schema.test.ts`]
+- AC10: For an entry promoted by a condition the validator requires the cited anchor to equal the declared one, a summary of at least 40 characters, and at least three distinct words of five or more letters that occur in the anchored section (as many as the section holds when it has fewer than three); each failure is reported as its own miss with the reason. +# Conditional mandatory reads for documents cited by project rules
+
+Status: draft (PRD and criteria wait for the operator; not frozen)
+Source: user description (origin: human-request)
+PRD: docs/requirements/keryx-conditional-reads/README.md
+Depends on: flow 461 (PR #1047). Rebase onto main once it is merged.
+
+## Problem
+
+Flow 461 made project rules mandatory reading for code and test workers. A document that a rule only cites (Vantage: STYLING.md about 100 KB, THEMING.md about 68 KB) is resolved as an optional on-demand contract with no condition. The validator never requires it, and nothing tells the worker when it matters. A task on className or theme tokens can pass every gate without the governing document being read.
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+A project declares, for each cited document, where it applies (file globs plus task keywords), the section that matters and a description. The resolver promotes matching documents from on_demand to must_read. The worker's result proves the read with the path, the sha256, the anchor and a summary. A deterministic validator checks that proof, warning first and blocking under the existing enforcement setting. The project can see gaps (undeclared citations, dead anchors, thin descriptions) from the CLI and the TUI.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- Запрос (дословно): «то есть я так понимаю что когда мы их импортируем в эти файлы которые идут в project rules должны не только ссылки хэши но и правильное грамотное описание чтобы агент мог понять и когда ему нужно читать основное правило и что он обязан его прочитать чтобы он сходил по ссылке именно вычитал» (source: helyx-channel message 212151, 2026-10-18T07:15:20Z (voice, transcribed); poll 211 answers)
+- Эффект (формализация агента): when a task touches a document's declared area, the worker cannot finish with a passing gate unless its result cites that document's declared section by hash and anchor with a summary that matches the section; an imported rule's cited documents carry a description saying when to read them.
+- Как наблюдать (предложение агента): resolve a fixture task on a styling file and see the document as must_read in the last-resolve record and in the TUI References tab; submit a result without the citation and see the validator miss; submit it with a summary unrelated to the section and see the summary miss; run the same task on an unrelated file and see the document stay on_demand with its description.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Proving a model really read the text (the check is a deterministic proxy, documented as such).
+- Model-inferred conditions; declarations are authored.
+- Changing rule selection, the cap default, or release/version bumps (releases are batched).
+- Rollout to other projects (operator).

 ### What `verify --bundled` checks, and what it does not
 
 `--bundled` is **layer one of three** and only layer one. It runs the checks that
 can be decided by reading files:

 |---|---|
 | `frontmatter:block` / `:name` / `:description` / `:metadata` | Required fields are present, non-empty, and `metadata` carries a `version`. |

+## 5. Make a long document required only when the task needs it
+
+A rule file is short and is read on every matching task. A document such as
+`STYLING.md` or `THEMING.md` is long, and rules usually point at it by name
+(``Follow `STYLING.md` for classes``). Left alone, such a document is listed
+`on_demand`, which no worker is checked on. You can declare when a document
+becomes required, and for which part of it.
+
+### Declare it
+
+Write `.metaproject/rules/project/references.json`. It is a separate file
+because rules are copied byte for byte and `keryx skills update --rules`
+overwrites them.
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema": 1,
+  "references": [
+    {
+      "path": "STYLING.md",
+      "when": {
+        "globs": ["src/**/*.css", "src/**/*.tsx"],
+        "keywords": ["className", "tailwind", "spacing"]
+      },
+      "anchor": "Class conventions",
+      "description": "Class naming, spacing and variants. Read before adding or changing className, CSS or inline style."
+    },
+    {
+      "path": "THEMING.md",
+      "when": { "globs": ["src/theme/**"], "keywords": ["theme", "dark mode", "colour"] },
+      "anchor": "Tokens",
+      "description": "Theme tokens and dark mode. Read before adding a colour or touching a theme."
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+- `path` is relative to the project root, with `/` separators, and stays inside
+  it.
+- `when` needs at least one glob or keyword. A glob is matched against the task's
+  files, as a rule's `globs` are.
+- A keyword is matched against the task text as a whole word, ignoring case. A
+  keyword may be several words (`dark mode`).
+- `anchor` (optional) is a heading in the document. Only that section is
+  required: from the heading to the next heading of the same or a higher level,
+  not counting headings inside fenced code. The heading matches by its text or
+  its slug, and the first match wins. Without `anchor` the whole file is required.
+- `description` is shown next to the entry, so a worker can see why it is there.
+- A property that is not listed here is an error.
+- Declare each document once, with one `anchor`. Two entries for the same path
+  (`STYLING.md` and `./STYLING.md` count as the same path) make the file
+  invalid, and the error names both entries.
+
+A missing `references.json` means no declarations. A malformed one does not stop
+anything: no reference is promoted, the resolver prints a warning, and the task
+carries on. The file is also covered by a JSON schema,
+`docs/requirements/keryx-conditional-reads/schemas/references.schema.json`.
+
+### Resolve against the task
+
+Pass the task text with `--task-text`. It is cut at 4000 characters, and the cut
+text is what `last.json` records. When the text is cut and a declaration has
+keywords, the resolve warns that a keyword after the cut cannot promote a
+reference. A task that edits `src/button.tsx`:
+
+```console
+$ keryx skills resolve-context --files src/button.tsx --for implement \
+    --task-text "Add a loading spinner to the Button"
+Budget: 462 of 131072 bytes (default)
+
+## must_read (2)
+- .metaproject/rules/project/styling.mdc — project rule, glob:src/**/*.tsx, 113 bytes, sha256 65a5c6fe816c
+- STYLING.md — project contract, condition:glob:src/**/*.tsx, 438 bytes, sha256 3b473b6d9c0e (anchor "Class conventions", section 349 bytes)
+
+## on_demand (1)
+- THEMING.md — project contract, declared, 152 bytes, sha256 169fe095b433 (anchor "Tokens", section 141 bytes)
+```
+
+`STYLING.md` moved to `must_read` because the file matches `src/**/*.tsx`. The
+reason, `condition:glob:<glob>` or `condition:keyword:<word>`, says which
+condition fired. `THEMING.md` stayed `on_demand`, reason `declared`.
+A task on `src/session.ts` with the text "Let the user pick a dark mode" promotes
+`THEMING.md` instead, with reason `condition:keyword:dark mode`. A task on the same file with
+the text "Fix the token refresh race" promotes neither.
+
+Details that can surprise you:
+
+- The byte count of a promoted document is the size of its section, or of the
+  file when there is no anchor. The size cap never moves a promoted document back
+  to `on_demand`; it prints a warning that the cap is exceeded instead, and the
+  budget line includes the promoted bytes.
+- An `anchor` that is not found falls back to the whole file, with a warning.
+- A declared file that is missing, outside the project, larger than 262144 bytes,
+  or already listed as a rule is left out, with a warning.
+- When a `references.json` exists, the result also lists `undeclared`: `.md`
+  documents that a project rule names but that have no declaration. A cited
+  `.mdc` file or a file under the rules folder is another rule and is not listed
+  there. A rule may spell the path `./STYLING.md`; it is the same document as
+  `STYLING.md`.
+
+### What the worker must return
+
+For a promoted document the worker's `project_context_applied` item carries two
+more fields, `anchor` and `summary`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "path": "STYLING.md",
+  "sha256": "3b473b6d9c0e…",
+  "how": "read",
+  "anchor": "Class conventions",
+  "summary": "Class names go through the cn helper, spacing uses the Tailwind scale, variants sit in a cva definition beside the component."
+}
+```
+
+`sha256` is the hash of the whole file, as printed by `resolve-context`, even
+when only a section was promoted. The checks run when the task is closed, or by
+hand with `keryx skills contracts validate result.json --schema
+task-implementer-output --resolved last.json`. For an item promoted by a
+condition, a miss is recorded when:
+
+1. `how` is `n/a`.
+2. `anchor` differs from the declared one.
+3. `summary` is shorter than 40 characters.
+4. `summary` shares fewer than three distinct words of five or more letters
+   with the section (or all of them, if the section holds fewer than three
+   such words). Words in any script count.
+
+A file that changed after it was resolved is counted separately, as drift. A
+miss is one line, and the headline counts both:
+
+```text
+project context: 1 miss(es), 0 drifted (enforcement warn)
+- project context miss: STYLING.md (condition:glob:src/**/*.tsx) has a summary that shares 0 distinct word(s) of 5 or more letters with the section "Class conventions"; 2 required. Write the summary in the wording of the text you read
+```
+
+Under `warn` this exits 0 and the task closes; under `block` it exits 1, the
+message goes to stderr, and `keryx flow task done` refuses.
+
+### Check the declarations
+
+```console
+$ keryx skills references check
+```
+
+It reads `references.json` and every rule in `.metaproject/rules/project/`, and
+ends with `N errors, M warnings`. It exits 1 on an error:
+
+| Finding | Level |
+|---------|-------|
+| `invalid-file`, `document-missing`, `document-outside-root`, `document-not-file`, `document-too-large`, `document-unreadable`, `anchor-not-found` | error |
+| `description-short` (under 20 characters), `keyword-short` (under 4) | warning |
+| `unused-declaration` (no project rule names the document), `undeclared-citation` (a rule names a document with no declaration), `rule-unreadable` | warning |
+
+A missing `references.json` is not an error. `--json` prints the same findings
+as JSON. The citation scan looks for backticked `X.md` names in project rules
+only: a rule imported with `--link` is not scanned, and neither are bundled
+rules.
+
+To start a file, `keryx skills references suggest` prints a skeleton for every
+document that a project rule names and `references.json` does not declare. It
+writes nothing. Copy the entries you want into `references.json`, fill in
+`description` and `when`, choose an `anchor` from `anchorCandidates`, and delete
+`anchorCandidates` and `bytes`, which the loader rejects as unknown properties.
+Delete an empty `globs` or `keywords` list as well; an empty one is an error.
+`keryx skills import
+--rules` ends with a reminder when it finds such documents.
+
+```console
+$ keryx skills references suggest
+{
+  "schema": 1,
+  "references": [
+    {
+      "path": "STYLING.md",
+      "bytes": 438,
+      "anchorCandidates": ["Styling", "Class conventions", "Cascade", "Inline style"],
+      "description": "",
+      "when": { "globs": [], "keywords": [] }
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+In the TUI, the sidebar line `refs <promoted>/<declared>` and the References tab
+of `/projectctx` (`/projectctx refs`) show the same state.
+
+### What this does not prove
+
+- **The proof is a proxy.** Keryx cannot see what an agent opened. A summary
+  passes when it has 40 characters and shares three distinctive words with the
+  section, and an agent that read nothing can sometimes do that: two sections
+  of a style guide easily share words such as "never" and "component". The check
+  catches a missing, empty or generic answer. It does not show that the agent
+  read the section.
+- **Breadth decides how often a document is required.** A glob such as `src/**`
+  or a keyword such as `component` promotes the document on most tasks. Use
+  narrow conditions, and let `references check` flag short keywords.
+- **A promoted document is never dropped for size.** If several are promoted
+  on one task, all of them are required and the cap only produces a warning.
+- **A malformed `references.json` turns the feature off** for that run. It warns
+  and does not block, so read the warnings.

+# Conditional mandatory reads for documents cited by project rules
+
+Flow: 462 (`.metaproject/flows/462-2026-10-18-conditional-reads/`). Status: DRAFT for the operator; criteria are not frozen.
+Criteria (single source): `.metaproject/flows/462-2026-10-18-conditional-reads/acceptance-criteria.md`.
+Builds on flow 461 (PR #1047, project rules first). This branch must be rebased on `main` once #1047 is merged; nothing here compiles without the 461 resolver.
+
+## 1. Problem
+
+Flow 461 made project rules `must_read` for code and test workers, and a validator compares what the worker cites with what the resolver required. Documents that a rule only points at are different. A Vantage rule such as `styling.mdc` says "see `STYLING.md`" (about 100 KB) and `THEMING.md` (about 68 KB). The resolver lists such a file as `kind: contract`, `tier: on_demand`, with no condition: it is always optional, the validator never asks for it, and the rule carries no statement of when the document matters. A worker that touches `className` or a theme token can finish with a green validator without having read the document that governs exactly that.
+
+The operator's wording (voice 212151): when a task intersects styling or theming the agent must read the project rule, and the same holds for the other rules; so the files imported into project rules need not just links and hashes but a proper description, so the agent understands when it must read the main document and that it must go to the link and actually read it.
+
+## 2. Decisions already taken by the operator (poll 211, 2026-10-18)
+
+| Question | Answer |
+|---|---|
+| When | a separate flow after green CI of #1047 (this flow) |
+| Condition shape | path masks of the task's files plus keywords of the task text, an anchor and a description per reference |
+| Effect of a match | the reference is promoted from `on_demand` to `must_read` |
+| Proof of reading | path, hash, anchor and a short summary |
+
+## 3. Goals
+
+1. A project declares, per cited document: where it applies (file globs and task keywords), which section matters (anchor), and a description of what the document governs.
+2. The resolver reads the declarations and the task, and promotes the matching documents to `must_read`; unmatched ones stay `on_demand` but now carry their description, so the worker can decide.
+3. The worker's result proves the read: path and sha256 as today, plus the anchor and a summary of the section.
+4. A validator checks the proof deterministically. A summary that has nothing to do with the section fails. It warns first and blocks under the existing `enforcement: block` setting.
+5. A project can see what is missing: undeclared citations, dead anchors, thin descriptions.
+6. All of it is visible in the TUI (sidebar, modal tab, command).
+
+## 4. Non-goals
+
+- Proving that a model actually read the text. The check is a deterministic proxy: the hash pins the version, the anchor pins the place, the summary must use the section's own vocabulary. It raises the cost of skipping the read; it cannot make it impossible. The docs say so.
+- Inferring conditions with a model. Declarations are authored (a human or an agent edits a file); `suggest` only prints a skeleton.
+- Reading whole 100 KB files up front. The anchor limits the obligation to one section.
+- Changing how rules themselves are selected (glob, `alwaysApply`) or the cap default.
+- Releasing (batched).
+
+## 5. Design
+
+### 5.1 Declarations
+
+A project file `.metaproject/rules/project/references.json` (schema committed under `docs/requirements/keryx-conditional-reads/schemas/`):
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema": 1,
+  "references": [
+    {
+      "path": "STYLING.md",
+      "when": { "globs": ["src/**/*.css", "src/**/*.tsx"], "keywords": ["className", "tailwind", "style", "spacing"] },
+      "anchor": "Class conventions",
+      "description": "Class naming and the Tailwind 4 cascade contract. Read before adding or changing className, CSS or inline style."
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+Why a sidecar and not front matter: rules are imported byte for byte from the upstream (`keryx skills import --rules`), so edits inside them are overwritten by `skills update`, and the front-matter reader is a flat YAML subset with no nested objects. The sidecar survives updates and is the project's own statement.
+
+`when.globs` use the same glob engine as rules. `when.keywords` are matched case-insensitively against the task text. A declaration with neither is invalid. A match on either is a match (a task can touch styling without touching a `.css` file, and the reverse).
+
+### 5.2 Resolution
+
+`resolve-context` takes the task text (`--task-text`, passed by the orchestrators from the task title and description; also a field of the shell/MCP operation). For each declared reference whose file exists and is cited or declared:
+
+- matched: `tier: must_read`, `reason: condition:glob|keyword (<rule or declaration>)`, plus `anchor`, `description`, `section_bytes`, `sha256` of the whole file;
+- not matched: `tier: on_demand`, with `description`, `anchor` and the condition, so the worker sees why it was not required.
+
+With an anchor, the obligation is the section from that heading to the next heading of the same or higher level, and the budget counts `section_bytes`, not the file. A matched reference is never demoted by the cap (an obligation that disappears when the budget is tight is the original bug); the existing over-cap warning fires instead. Citations without a declaration behave exactly as in flow 461.
+
+### 5.3 Proof
+
+`project_context_applied` items gain optional `anchor` and `summary`. They are required for entries promoted by a condition. `how` keeps its enum (`read|followed|n/a`) so every existing result stays valid. The validator, in addition to the path and hash check of flow 461, requires: the anchor equals the declared one; the summary has at least 40 characters; it contains at least three distinct words of five or more letters that occur in the anchored section. A miss is reported with the reason; `enforcement: block` makes it exit 1, and `flow task done` refuses it as for other misses.
+
+### 5.4 Authoring help
+
+- `keryx skills references check`: two declarations of one normalised path (error, naming both), undeclared citations (warning), declared file missing or outside the root or over the size limit (error), anchor not found (error), description under 20 characters (warning), declaration that no rule cites and that has no globs/keywords match possible (warning).
+- `keryx skills references suggest`: prints a JSON skeleton for every undeclared citation: path, size, the headings found as anchor candidates, empty `description`. Writes nothing.
+- `keryx skills import --rules` ends with the count of undeclared citations and the command to run.
+
+### 5.5 TUI
+
+Sidebar `ProjectCtx` gains `refs <promoted>/<declared>` after a resolve. The `/projectctx` modal gets a References tab: each declaration with its condition, anchor, whether the last resolve promoted it and why, and the problems `check` found. `/projectctx refs` opens it. The tab refreshes when a new resolve is recorded. The state matrix goes to `TUI-states.md` of this folder.
+
+## 6. Risks
+
+| Risk | Handling |
+|---|---|
+| Keywords too broad promote everything and fill the cap | the obligation is one anchored section, not the file; the over-cap warning and the Last resolve tab show the cost; keywords are the project's own and `check` flags a keyword shorter than 4 characters |
+| Keywords too narrow miss a real case | glob is an independent trigger; the unmatched reference stays listed with its description |
+| Summary check false positive (non-English section, very short section) | words are compared case-insensitively on letters of any script; a section with fewer than three qualifying words requires only as many shared words as it holds (none: only the length rule); warn mode first |
+| A worker fabricates a plausible summary | possible; the check raises the cost and the journal keeps the summary for review. Stated in the docs, not hidden |
+| Declarations drift from the documents | `check` reports dead anchors; the hash pin catches edits between resolve and validate (AC13) |
+

+
+A live run on vantage-frontend is an operator run with a runbook (AC18), like AC22 of flow 461. Rollout to the other projects stays with the operator.
